handoffPurpose: Capture the expanded skill tree map UX pass.
currentUserGoal: Make the skill tree feel huge instead of cramped, add a minimap like the playing field, show skills more zoomed in, add a hover visual on skill nodes, and add a crisp satisfying sound when selecting/upgrading a skill.

workCompleted.summary: Converted the skill tree from a fit-to-panel diagram into a clipped, pannable, wheel-zoomable skill map layer with its own camera.
Added a lightweight skill minimap that draws visible skill nodes, connections, selected/available state, and the current viewport marker.
Added a pooled hover ring visual for skill nodes and cleaned up hover/drag state when closing the skill tree.
Added a dedicated crisp skill selection sound cue and plays it when node/button selection attempts happen.
Fixed a mobile header spacing edge case where long skill resource text could crowd the status line and map.

knownIssuesOrDesignQuestions: The skill minimap is visual-only for now; dragging the main map and wheel zooming are implemented, but clicking the minimap to jump the camera is not.
The stress perf overlay can visually cover the top of the skill map on narrow/mobile debug runs. This is debug-only and not normal gameplay UI.
The new skill map camera focuses the selected or ready skill on open. Hovering another visible node updates selection/minimap state but does not auto-pan the camera.
recommendedNextSteps: Manually try the skill tree on the user's real save after deploying, especially panning/zooming between far branches.
Consider making the skill minimap clickable/drag-to-jump if players expect the same behavior as the world map.
If more skill branches are added, keep the minimap draw lightweight and avoid per-frame redraws.
doNotRevert: Do not restore the old fit-entire-tree layout; the user explicitly wanted the skill tree to feel huge and zoomed in.
Keep skill map pan/zoom work isolated to the skill overlay so board zoom/pan cannot happen underneath while the skill tree is open.
Keep skill hover visuals pooled on existing node objects instead of creating new graphics on every hover.
